Users can view affected locations, access information about fire events, and understand how surrounding ecosystems may be impacted.

Astera Watch is important because wildfire damage does not end when the fire is extinguished. Understanding its lasting effects is essential for environmental research and better-informed decisions. details:
Project Details – Astera Watch

Astera Watch is a satellite-based wildfire monitoring and environmental impact analysis platform. It uses satellite observations and AI-powered models to identify potential fire-affected areas, analyze changes in the surrounding landscape, and provide information about the environmental impacts of fire events.

How It Works

The platform brings fire-related information and satellite-based analysis into one web application. Users can explore potential fire locations on an interactive map, examine detected surface changes, and access information about affected areas and their possible environmental consequences.

Astera Watch also includes a dedicated Research Center where scientists can organize research projects, explore datasets, and study specific fire-affected locations. This connects satellite analysis with scientific investigation.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Wildfires can leave long-lasting damage even after the flames disappear. Astera Watch aims to make this damage easier to explore and understand, support environmental research, and provide a shared space for studying fire events and their consequences.

Our long-term vision is to develop a growing reference platform for wildfire events and environmental damage. Future plans include a mobile application for alerts to citizens and researchers, researcher-contributed datasets, geographic annotations, published studies, and expert-reviewed scientific contributions. These contributions could also help improve the training and validation of future AI models.

Tools and Technologies

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, and Vite.
  • Backend foundation: Python and FastAPI.
  • Spatial database technology: PostgreSQL and PostGIS.
  • Data sources and research: NASA NISAR, NASA FIRMS, MODIS MCD64A1, Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2, and Natural Earth geographic data.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Astera Watch goes beyond displaying fire locations. Its creative approach connects three important stages: detecting potential fire-affected areas, understanding their environmental impacts, and enabling scientists to investigate those areas further.

Our team considered scientific reliability, satellite-data limitations, accessibility, usability, and the different needs of ordinary users and researchers. We also considered the importance of distinguishing actual observations from demo data and potential detections from confirmed fire events.

The current web prototype provides the interface and browser-based research workflows. Live data integrations, fully validated end-to-end analysis, mobile alerts, community data contributions, and expert review are planned future developments.
